content.text: Erase the narrowest ellipse without touching other itmes using Eraser tool in Excalidraw.
I'll help you erase the narrowest ellipse in Excalidraw. Let me first take a screenshot to see the current state of the canvas.
I can see multiple overlapping ellipses on the canvas. Let me zoom in to better identify the narrowest ellipse (the one with the smallest width relative to its height).

Let me try the zoom with a different region format.

I can see there's a very narrow, tall ellipse (almost vertical, thin ellipse) in the center-left area. Let me get a clearer view of the whole picture to identify all ellipses and find the narrowest one.

Now I can clearly see the ellipses. There is a very narrow (thin, tall) vertical ellipse in the left-center area. This narrow ellipse spans vertically and is quite thin in width - it's the narrowest one. 

In the original screenshot coordinates, this narrow vertical ellipse is located roughly around x=630, spanning from y≈290 (top) to y≈510 (bottom), with its narrowest part around x=615-645.

To use the Eraser tool, I need to click on the actual stroke of this narrow ellipse without touching other ellipses. Let me first select the Eraser tool.

The Eraser tool is now selected (highlighted in the toolbar, and the message says "Hold Alt to revert the elements marked for deletion").

Now I can clearly see the narrow vertical ellipse. It's the thin, tall ellipse in the center that spans from about y=285 at the top to y=510 at the bottom, with its narrowest width around x=615-650. The top point of this narrow ellipse is around (640, 285) and it curves down.

To erase only this narrow ellipse without touching others, I need to click on a part of its stroke that's isolated from other ellipses. The best spot would be near the top or bottom tip of the narrow ellipse where it's less crowded. 

Looking carefully, the top tip of the narrow ellipse is around (640, 287) and the bottom tip is around (632, 508). Let me examine the isolated parts. The bottom tip around (632, 505) appears to be a relatively clear spot. Let me click precisely on the stroke of this narrow ellipse near its bottom tip.

The narrow, thin vertical ellipse has been successfully erased. Comparing the before and after screenshots:

- **Before:** There was a very thin, tall vertical ellipse running through the center of the drawing (spanning from around y=285 to y=510).
- **After:** That narrow vertical ellipse is now gone, while all the other rounder/wider ellipses remain intact.

The eraser click also shows the undo button is now active (bottom left), confirming the deletion was performed. The narrowest ellipse has been erased successfully without affecting any of the other overlapping ellipses.
